extracted.intended_audience: students, mathematicians, and general readers interested in the concept and history of mathematical rigor
extracted.subtask_description: Describe the standards, methods, and stylistic norms that constitute mathematical rigor (axiomatic method, precise definitions, rigorous proofs, presentation style) and their historical development. Intended as a conceptual/style guide rather than a scoring rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: axiomatische Vorgehensweise / scharfe Definitionen
rubrics_metrics.description: „axiomatische Vorgehensweise anhand scharfer Definitionen“ — Verwendung von klaren, sharply stated axioms and precise definitions as the foundation for mathematical work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes adopting an axiomatic approach with sharp definitions (example: Euclid's Elements). This is presented as a core component of mathematical rigor: define concepts precisely before using them. Anti-pattern: relying on vague or informal notions rather than explicit definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: zwingende Beweise (rigorous/compelling proofs)
rubrics_metrics.description: „zwingende Beweise“ — proofs must be compelling and logically conclusive, not heuristic or merely persuasive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigor requires that results be justified by proofs that leave no essential logical gap. Historically stressed by Cauchy, Weierstraß, Hilbert. Anti-patterns include intuitive arguments without justification and appeals to unproven heuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: systematische Deduktion
rubrics_metrics.description: „Methode der systematischen Deduktion“ — deriving results by systematic logical deduction from stated premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical reasoning should proceed by deductive chains rather than empirical or ad-hoc argument. Encouraged to organize arguments into clear deductive steps; avoid leaps of inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: endliche logische Schlüsse aus endlicher Anzahl von Voraussetzungen (Hilbert's requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hilbert: the correctness of an answer must be demonstrated "durch eine endliche Anzahl von Schlüssen, und zwar auf Grund einer endlichen Anzahl von Voraussetzungen, welche in der Problemstellung liegen und die jedesmal genau zu formulieren sind."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require a finite sequence of logical inferences based on a finite set of explicitly formulated assumptions. Guidance: state assumptions exactly and show derivation in finitely many steps. Anti-pattern: hidden or ill-defined hypotheses; arguments relying on an unbounded or ill-specified chain of reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Klarheit der Begriffe und Behauptungen
rubrics_metrics.description: „Die Mathematik fordert Klarheit der Begriffe und Behauptungen und duldet keinen Nebel und keine unbeweisbaren Erklärungen.“
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand clear statements of concepts and claims; avoid vague language and assertions that cannot be proved. Examples: precise theorem statements, explicitly stated hypotheses. Anti-patterns: nebulous phrasing, informal claims presented as facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundanzfreiheit (eliminate superfluous statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: „Redundanzfreiheit: Alle überflüssigen Aussagen sollen eliminiert werden und das Verständnis des Gesagten wird dem Leser überlassen (sachliche Richtigkeit und Wichtigkeit vorausgesetzt)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation should avoid superfluous, personally colored additions; include only theorem statements, assumptions, proof steps, and minimal justificatory remarks (e.g., why a result matters). Guidance notes both usefulness and a downside: strict redundancy-freedom can harm understandability. Anti-patterns: long personal digressions or unnecessary motivation inside formal proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satz–Beweis–Korollar Präsentationsstil (minimal motivation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gauss' style: works written in the form 'Satz–Beweis–Korollar' that contain no motivation of the chosen proof directions and often hide the way discoveries were made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A common rigorous stylistic norm is to present results in the concise theorem-proof-corollary format, omitting narrative motivation for how proofs were discovered. Guidance: keep exposition focused on formal correctness; be aware this can make texts less accessible to readers seeking intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigoröse Begründung für zuvor intuitive Methoden
rubrics_metrics.description: Restore rigorous foundations for methods that were previously justified only intuitively (e.g., the rigorous foundations for infinitesimal calculus by Cauchy and Weierstraß).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working with formerly heuristic or intuitive methods, provide precise definitions and proofs that place them on a secure foundation. Example: formalizing limits and continuity in analysis. Anti-pattern: continuing to rely on informal intuition without formal underpinning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strenge als Mittel zur Einfachheit und Weiterentwickelbarkeit
rubrics_metrics.description: Hilbert's claim: striving for rigor often leads to simpler, more comprehensible, and more developable methods rather than being the enemy of simplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat rigor not as an end in itself but as a tool to find simpler, more generalizable proofs and methods. Guidance: prefer rigorous approaches that also clarify and simplify arguments; avoid conceiving rigor as mere pedantry.
